Every basaltic shield volcano is built m.why: The make-up of shield volcanoes is stated directly and often (the textbook contrast with ash-built stratovolcanoes and cinder cones). The class is basaltic shields because Wikipedia notes the term is 'at times' applied to rarer pyroclastic shields built from fragmentary material (Billy Mitchell, Purico), which would be real exceptions to a rule about all shields; basaltic shields, the usual sense, have none.

sources.quote: It is formed by the eruption of highly fluid (low viscosity) lava
Although the term is generally applied to basaltic shields, it has also at times been applied to rarer scutiform volcanoes of differing magmatic composition
sources.note: Pyroclastic shields are the exception the narrower class avoids.

sources.quote: Although most shield volcanoes are by volume almost entirely Hawaiian and basaltic in origin, they are rarely exclusively so.

Mauna Loa is a basaltic shield volcano..why: Stated by name very often, and Wikipedia ties its shape to its fluid lava by name, which is what makes the by-name world reasonable.

notes: Delete mirroring geography-replace-0007: removes the rule that basaltic shield volcanoes are built mainly from fluid lava. New members named in the prompt are does-not-know (determinate); Mauna Loa and Kīlauea keep their lava make-up if stored by name and are does-not-know if reached through the rule. Changed in verification: (1) the class is narrowed from shield volcanoes to basaltic shield volcanoes, because Wikipedia's Shield volcano article names pyroclastic shields (Billy Mitchell, Purico) built from fragmentary material, real exceptions to 'every shield volcano is built mainly from fluid lava'; Mauna Loa and Kīlauea are basaltic shields. 'Basaltic' leans toward lava but does not state the answer (basaltic ash and cinder cones exist), an accepted R2 risk. (2) The new members Erta Ale (famous lava lake, 'Erta Ale AND lava' 3,390 approximate) and Piton de la Fournaise ('AND lava flows' 1,232) were replaced by obscure Icelandic shields, since their lava make-up is likely stored by name.
